transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: 2025-11-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ravi Singh (Redwood SE), Evan Brooks (VectorLane Head of ML), Priya Kapoor (VectorLane Platform Eng), Michael O'Neal (VectorLane PM)

Summary:
Quick scoping call to align on POC success criteria and workload characterization for a routing / logistics NLP assistant. Customer wants a pilot to validate throughput (QPS), latency SLOs at peak, and unit cost per 1M tokens using VectorLane's token distribution. Next steps: share traces, Redwood to propose benchmark harness and schedule dedicated pilot run.

Topics: QPS profiles (steady, daily peaks, burst), concurrency patterns, input vs output token distributions, failover (fallback to smaller model), quality regression tolerance, telemetry needed for cost modeling.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll just do intros real quick, I'm Maya, AE on this one and Ravi's our SE who will lead the perf side.
[00:07] Evan: Evan here, Head of ML at VectorLane. Priya and Michael are with me.
[00:12] Priya: hi all.
[00:14] Michael: Hey.
[00:16] Ravi: Cool, so goal for today is to nail down the workload profile so we can size a POC, run benchmarks and give you cost numbers.
[00:25] Evan: Yep, we want to see if Redwood can hit our p95 latency targets under the real traffic shape. Our current infra does embeddings + response gen across two models, and we have some spikes during route planning windows.
[00:36] Priya: to give some context, our production is about 800 qps average for the microservice powering the assistant, but that includes a lot of cached hits. Uncached requests are closer to 40 qps baseline, with ad hoc bursts up to 1200 qps during peak batch planning windows, which last 2–4 minutes.
[00:53] Maya: that's helpful. When you say cached hits, are you referring to an OKTA of in-process cache? just to be precise when we model KV cache.
[01:01] Priya: yeah, it's a combination of an LRU prefix cache and Redis for session-level caching. We usually have like 60% cache hit for repeated route prompts.
[01:10] Ravi: good — prefix cache will change the effective token load a lot because cache hits often bypass the full model. For sizing we need a sample of the token distribution: median input tokens, 95th input tokens, and median output. Can you share anonymized traces?
[01:22] Evan: we'll share a 7-day sample. Quick numbers off the top: median input ~ 25 tokens, p95 input ~ 160 tokens, median output ~ 120 tokens, p95 output ~ 720 tokens. Those p95 outputs tend to come from multi-turn planning sessions.
[01:36] Michael: also worth noting we sometimes invoke tools so the model response gets longer when external calls are aggregated.
[01:42] Ravi: noted. For the POC we usually ask customers to define success criteria across three axes: latency SLO (p95), throughput (sustained QPS) and cost per 1M tokens or per 1k reqs, and optionally quality delta relative to your baseline. What's your SLO target?
[01:56] Evan: we aim p95 < 450ms for the generation path when uncached at our baseline traffic; during the big 2–4 minute spikes we'd accept p95 up to 800ms if throughput is maintained.
[02:09] Priya: and we want tail latencies not to exceed 2s even in worst-case fallback.
[02:14] Maya: that seems reasonable. For the benchmark harness we'll model two phases: 1) steady-state: 40 uncached qps with input/output token distribution you described; 2) spike simulation: ramp to 1200 qps over 30s, hold for 3 minutes, then ramp down, measure p50/p95/p99 and failures.
[02:32] Evan: do you simulate KV cache hit rates? That changes throughput a lot.
[02:36] Ravi: yes — we can parameterize cache hit at 60% and run variants at 20/40/60/80% to show sensitivity. We'll also model prefix caching behaviors which reduce compute per request.
[02:47] Priya: what about batching? our service is latency-sensitive, so we don't want batching to hurt p95, but some micro-batching may be acceptable during peaks.
[02:56] Ravi: we have continuous batching in the runtime — it batches only when it helps latency for throughput workloads. For this POC we'll test with batching disabled, then enable smart batching and show tradeoffs; we'll quantify added latency vs cost reduction.
[03:08] Michael: can you also include a fallback model path? if the big model is saturated we want automatic fallback to a smaller v2 model with degraded quality but consistent latency.
[03:16] Maya: Yes, Redwood supports routing policies and automatic fallbacks. We'll include a canary policy in the test: above X% saturated we'll route new requests to the smaller model and measure quality delta.
[03:26] Evan: How do you measure quality? we have our own BLEU-ish metric and business KPIs — it's not just token logprob.
[03:32] Ravi: we can run the same prompt set against both models and produce a pairwise diff, but we'll rely on your evaluation harness for business KPIs; we can export outputs for your eval.
[03:39] Priya: ok. On telemetry we need per-route token counts, per-request latency (end-to-end and model-only), and cost per token.
[03:46] Maya: Redwood Console exposes token-level breakdowns and per-route dashboards — we'll capture these metrics during the runs and provide CSV/metrics export.
[03:53] Evan: about timeline — how long to get benchmark numbers if we share traces tomorrow?
[03:57] Ravi: once we have traces and your canonical prompt set, we estimate 7–10 business days to run synthetic benchmarks (different cache hit curves, batching configs, and region routing), plus 2–3 days to collate dashboards and a write-up. So around 2 weeks total.
[04:12] Michael: great. And pricing for a pilot — we want to understand Dedicated vs hosted cost if we run a pilot at production-ish QPS for a month.
[04:21] Maya: we'll sketch two options: hosted POC (usage-based) and a short-term Dedicated reservation for the pilot window. Pricing sketch will include token cost projection and an estimated infra surcharge for Dedicated.
[04:32] Evan: what about data residency and logs? we need audit logs for compliance.
[04:36] Maya: Redwood Private/Dedicated options support audit logs and can be deployed in VPC; we can set retention windows and integrate with KMS. We'll attach the security datasheet.
[04:45] Priya: some of our traffic originates in EU and US; can you route regionally?
[04:49] Ravi: yes — routing by region is supported; for the POC we can simulate multi-region ingress and show latencies.
[04:55] Evan: for the actual benchmark, how do you model concurrency? our service has long-lived websocket connections for multi-turn, so simultaneous KV cache reads and generation happen.
[05:03] Ravi: we model concurrency as the number of in-flight model sessions; in your case multi-turn websocket sessions with retained KV cache increase active context and KV working set. We'll simulate session churn and long-lived contexts in the harness.
[05:15] Michael: any constraints we should know about for reproducibility? e.g., tokenization differences across models, sampling seeds, or streaming vs non-streaming affects latencies.
[05:24] Ravi: good point — we'll use your model family equivalent in Redwood's catalog where possible; otherwise we'll note tokenizer variance and run normalized tests. We'll include both streaming and non-streaming runs.
[05:33] Evan: okay let's define POC success criteria explicitly: 1) p95 uncached generation <= 450ms at baseline 40 qps; 2) during 1200 qps burst p95 <= 800ms and error rate < 1%; 3) cost per 1M tokens not exceed $X (we'll fill X after we get tokenization mapping); 4) telemetry availability and export of audit logs.
[05:53] Maya: I'll capture that and include in the POC doc.
[05:57] Priya: will you run tests against our replicas or do you run in Redwood environment?
[06:01] Ravi: typically we run in Redwood-hosted environment with traffic profile shaped to match your traces. For a Dedicated pilot we can also run in your VPC with the Private control plane.
[06:10] Michael: do you simulate network jitter and tail compounding like slow external tool responses?
[06:15] Ravi: yes — we can inject synthetic downstream tool latency and measure end-to-end tail.
[06:20] Evan: what's the retention for logs in the POC? we may want 30 days.
[06:24] Maya: default is 7 days in hosted POC but we can extend to 30 with access to the retention add-on — we'll call that out.
[06:31] Priya: anything else on telemetry? we want cost attribution per feature flag because different routes have different model sizes.
[06:37] Ravi: the console can break down cost per route/model and tag by feature flag; we'll show an example report.
[06:43] Michael: sweet. So next actions are 1) VectorLane sends traces and canonical prompts, 2) Redwood produces benchmark plan and pricing sketch, 3) sync in two weeks for results.
[06:53] Maya: yep. I'll create a short POC spec doc and share a calendar invite for a benchmark review.
[06:58] Evan: thanks.
[07:00] Priya: thanks all.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription occasionally rendered 'KV cache' as 'K-V cash' and 'Redwood Dedicated' as 'Redwood dedicate' in the raw export; manual check applied but some small errors remain.

Attachments mentioned: link to POC template (shared via Drive), security datasheet (to be attached), sample benchmark spreadsheet (Ravi to generate).

End of transcript.
